entries.value: "`bsc ear` — always-on local capture: segments a live microphone into speech-only audio within a retention bound it enforces rather than documents."

lead: # The incident model — the ear raises Detections into the same ledger the network sensors use.
# Shared SQLite open + busy_timeout plumbing (the `conn` feature) — so a CLI write never races the app.
# The baseline is accumulated HABIT, so it has to outlive the invocation that measured it —
# and it is keyed per (speaker, channel), which is a query rather than a file read.
# Cross-platform capture. On Linux this is the ALSA backend, which is why libasound2-dev is a build
# prerequisite for this crate and for nothing else in the workspace.
# WAV read/write. Segments are wav rather than raw so they are inspectable with any player and
# readable by whisper tooling without a decoder of our own.
# For silencing ALSA's own diagnostics at the fd level while enumerating. Already in the tree via
# cpal -> alsa, so this makes a transitive dependency direct rather than adding one.
# Learned speech denoiser (pure-Rust RNNoise port): no model download, no C, no ort. Handles the
# non-stationary rain/handling noise that spectral subtraction cannot. RNNoise operates at 48kHz.
# DeepFilterNet3 clarity engine: ort runs the fused ONNX graph (same runtime as bsc-say/Kokoro);
# realfft does the 960-point real STFT the model requires (not a power of two, so the crate radix-2
# FFT cannot; realfft is what libDF itself uses).
# The ear's DURABLE tunnel identity uses the SAME Noise IK keypair generator the desktop app
# does, so a phone pins one kind of key whichever it paired with. This crate is Tauri-free and
# snow-only: NO relay client, no websocket stack and no async runtime enters bsc-ear with it.
# The keychain-backed vault that identity is persisted through — its `Vault` trait, injected as a
# trait object so the logic is testable against an in-memory fake. Reusing it keeps ONE secret
# store on this machine instead of minting a parallel one for the ear.
# The pairing payload's encodings, matched to the app's: STANDARD (padded) for hostPubKey, which
# is what the mobile client decodes and length-checks, and URL_SAFE_NO_PAD for the room id, which
# is what the relay's validateRoomId accepts. Versions track src-tauri's so both ends agree.
